sections.teaching:
The prof's lecture PPTs, supplementary notes and discussion questions were not organized in 1 single place. He would jump from PPT to the notes and then back to the PPT. So it's best if you have all the lecture materials ready before class.

During class, you would have to copy down everything he wrote on the whiteboard, because these would be highly likely to come up in the exam.

The prof is a hilarious guy. He applies business law to everyday life.
sections.grading:
Group research paper: 20%
Mid Term: 35%  (Mean: 33.9 and SD: 6.51 )
Final Exam: 35%
Class participation: 10%

Mid-term and Final were all short questions and essays. No MCs. You're allowed to bring a 2-sided A4 cheat sheet. As long as you copy all the legal principles and relevant examples, you should be able to handle the exams. Also, the questions were mainly based on the discussion questions + the notes he wrote on the whiteboard, i.e. extra points that were NOT on the PPT.

For the Mid Term, there were 2 essay questions on exemption clause and contract law respectively. They resemble the discussion questions in class.

For the Final, there were short questions about ethical issues such as minimum wage.

There's no absolute right or wrong in law as long as you could back your argument with legal principles. So for the essay part, try to elaborate your point with legal principles with examples.

I don't think we did particularly well in the Paper. Got around 1.7 SD above mean in Mid term. Don't know the results for Final. In the end, got A+.
sections.workload:

sections.content:
The topics are incredibly interesting if you'd like to understand a bit of the basics of business law. The course covers the fundamentals of each topic (Basic concepts of law, the legal system in HK/China, contract law, employment law, tort law and business ethics).

You don't need to be afraid of the course code - trust me. I chose this course last semester because there was really nothing else to take. I thought it'd be awful but it turned out to be the best course choice by far.
sections.teaching:
Charles is super friendly and likes to make lots of jokes (though no one laughs). He uses powerpoints and a ton of word documents that contain 'past paper questions'. A typical class consists of him going through the powerpoints and then applies the concepts you just learned in the questions. You can feel free to interrupt him at any point in time to ask questions - he's always happy to clarify.

Attendance is not compulsory even though there are 'participation points'. BUT if you want to do well (which I presume you do), you NEED TO GO TO CLASS. Charles' PPT & notes (which he uploads to LMES) are not comprehensive enough. He often adds additional information. If you're a fan of taking a lot of notes and then exactly regurgitating everything the professor says then this is the class for you, seriously.
sections.grading:
The grading is pretty fair to be honest.
Mid term 35%
Final 35%
Participation 10%
Group Project 20%

The group project is the really long essay you write (with other people) on a law topic. You draw this topic out of a hat with the TA. You can then go to Charles and arrange a meeting and pretend you are honestly very confused and hopeless. He will then tell you exactly what he wants in the essay - no joke. He's the nicest person on earth.

The 10% participation is a mixture of your questions in class and the verbal presentation you give with your group mates for the group project. Throughout the entire semester I think I asked about two questions... so honestly it doesn't really matter. I've been told that so long as you give the presentation, you get the full 10%.

The final exam was a mind blower because half of the paper was on Confucius. We learned business ethics in the last two weeks of the semester and Charles so happened to focus on business ethics for the final. A lot of people thought memorizing business ethics was a waste of their time and didn't revise for it... so... oops?

I got 41/50 for the midterm - slightly above mean. He never told us what we got for the group project or final or for participation. I ended up getting an A+.

But I assure you that the exam questions are EXACTLY like the past paper questions he goes through in class (except 1 exam question = past paper question 1 + 2 + 3 combined). If you pay attention to class you will get a good grade.

sections.content: The topics are quite interesting but also easy to follow, if you can put effort. The course introduces you with the basic concepts of law, such as the legal system in Hong Kong, the employment law, the tort law, the contract law, and the business ethics. It must be emphasized, although the course is with the course code above 3000, it is only an introduction to law. So, it is okay for you to pick the topics up. The most important thing is your effort.
sections.teaching: The instructor is a good one. Not only can he explain the abstract concepts of laws clearly with a variety of examples in real-life, but he sometimes makes some jokes so that the lessons are not boring at all. He can cater to the needs of the students, and he welcomes questions. Actually, what is the most important in the lessons is not the notes he distribute, but what he has discussed in the lessons.

The mean was 38 and the S.D was not shown. I guessed my mark was below 1.5 S.D. My group project was fair. And I guessed I did my final very good because overall I got a B grade.

The examinations cover not only the power-point notes but also what has been discussed in the lessons. So, it is important to attend all the lessons and even take down the notes of what the instructor says. The workload for preparing the examinations is huge. Also, for the group project, the topics are too broad, and it is quite demanding to work on this, especially if you are not interested in the topics. The final thing to say is that if you have the enthusiasm in law, let's take the course, but otherwise, don't risk your GPA.
